agent.problem: Cards 4, 10 and 11 use "their" or "them" without identifying the people, and card 6 begins with "that oath" even though its antecedent was on the preceding story card. These questions rely on cards that are no longer visible instead of supplying their own context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The earlier cards give no basis for choosing "gods" over "kings" or "nations." The baker must guess the unrevealed wording of verse 10 rather than reason out its meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Card 8 does not identify who "these people" are, card 12 refers back to "that beautiful olive tree" without establishing the picture in the question, and card 13 does not identify who "the people" are. These questions are not self-contained once the preceding story cards disappear.
